explain.say: Ancient torsion catapults, like the Roman onager, stored energy in a thick bundle of twisted rope or animal sinew. The throwing arm was pushed through the middle of the bundle.

explain.say: Soldiers used a winch to pull the arm down, which twisted the bundle even tighter. All the work they did was stored as elastic energy, like a twisted rubber band.

faq.q: Why does a catapult need a winch?
faq.a: Twisting the rope bundle takes a huge force. A winch with a long handle and ratchet lets a few soldiers pull the arm down bit by bit and hold it there.
asks: How did soldiers pull the catapult arm back?

faq.q: Where does a catapult store its energy?
faq.a: In the twisted bundle of rope or sinew. Twisting it stores elastic potential energy, which is released when the arm is let go.
asks: Why did catapults use twisted rope?

faq.q: How does the arm throw the stone?
faq.a: The untwisting bundle swings the arm up fast, carrying the stone in its cup or sling. When the arm hits the crossbar and stops, the stone carries on by itself.
asks: Why does the stone leave the arm?

faq.q: What makes the stone fly in a curve?
faq.a: Once released, the only big force on the stone is gravity, pulling it down while it keeps moving forward. So it follows a curved path called a parabola, apart from air resistance.
asks: Why does a thrown stone curve down?

faq.q: What is the difference between a catapult and a trebuchet?
faq.a: A torsion catapult stores energy in twisted rope; a counterweight trebuchet uses a heavy falling weight on a long lever arm. Trebuchets came later and threw heavier stones.

facts: Greek and Roman torsion engines used twisted bundles of animal sinew or hair rope to store energy.
Ignoring air, a thrown object travels furthest when launched at 45 degrees.

quiz.say: In a torsion catapult, what kind of energy is stored before launch?
quiz.show: In a torsion catapult, what kind of energy is stored before launch?
quiz.why: Twisting the rope bundle stores elastic potential energy, like a wound spring.

wrong.1: No fuel is burned; the energy comes from twisting.
wrong.2: Sound is made at launch, not stored.
